title: Desk Figure Note — Premium Build, Cover Dates, Waiting Period and Term Allowance on the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans
content:
The premium of a plan under the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans is built unit by unit from the tier's price for each covered unit's equipment type; a type priced at zero for a tier cannot be enrolled on that tier. Cover begins on the day the owner accepts the quote, runs for the tier's coverage term, and claims may be filed only after the tier's waiting period has passed from the first day of cover. At the start of each cover term the plan is credited with the tier's per-term claim cap as its allowance; the allowance does not carry forward. A unit added mid-term is priced pro rata by whole months remaining and serves its own waiting period from the day it is added. A unit removed mid-term is refunded pro rata by whole months remaining, less any claim already paid on that unit in the term.

## The premium as a quantity

The annual premium is the total, over every covered unit, of the tier's annual price for that unit's equipment type, stated to the cent. A unit of a type whose price on the tier is zero is not enrolled on that tier, and contributes nothing to any premium.

### Worked figure on hypothetical units

Two rooftop units and one air handler quoted on the Parts & Labor Protection Plan, where the rate card gives 640 USD for a rooftop unit and 520 USD for an air handler:

| Unit | Type | Annual price on the tier |
|---|---|---|
| Unit one | Rooftop unit | 640 USD |
| Unit two | Rooftop unit | 640 USD |
| Unit three | Air handler | 520 USD |
| **Premium** | | **1800 USD per year** |

The same three units on the Manufacturer Warranty Registration, every type being priced at zero there, give no premium and, on the same clause, no enrollment of those types at that tier.

## Cover dates and the waiting period

| Quantity | Definition |
|---|---|
| First day of cover | The day the owner accepts the quote. |
| Cover term | The tier's coverage term, in calendar months, running from the first day of cover. |
| Day from which a claim may be filed | The day the tier's waiting period, in calendar days from the first day of cover, has passed. |

A unit added mid-term serves its own waiting period from the day it is added, whatever the plan's own waiting period end.

## The term allowance

At the start of each cover term the plan's allowance is credited with the tier's per-term claim cap. What remains of the allowance at the end of the term does not carry forward: the new term opens at the tier's per-term cap and no more. On the Parts & Labor Protection Plan, whose per-term ceiling is 15000 USD, a plan that closes its term with 4000 USD of allowance unused opens the next term with 15000 USD, not 19000 USD.

## Units added or removed mid-term, worked on hypothetical figures

- **Added.** A rooftop unit (640 USD per year on the Parts & Labor Protection Plan, a 12 month term) added with 5 whole months remaining is priced at 640 USD multiplied by 5 and divided by 12, that is 266.67 USD, and may have a claim filed on it only after its own waiting period has passed from the day it was added.
- **Removed.** An air handler (520 USD per year on the same tier and term) removed with 4 whole months remaining, on which 90 USD of claim has already been paid in the term, is refunded 520 USD multiplied by 4 and divided by 12, that is 173.33 USD, less the 90 USD already paid: 83.33 USD.
- Months are counted whole; a part month remaining does not count toward the proportion.
